title: Running Data Workloads on Kubernetes (Jobs & CronJobs)

scenes.heading: Jobs & CronJobs on Kubernetes
scenes.subheading: Run batch and scheduled data workloads
scenes.narration: Not every workload runs forever; Kubernetes Jobs and CronJobs are built for batch and scheduled data tasks that run to completion.

scenes.heading: Deployment vs Job
scenes.narration: A deployment is designed for long-running services that should stay alive indefinitely and restart whenever they stop. A Job is the opposite: it runs a task to completion, retries on failure up to a limit, and tracks how many successful completions it has achieved. That distinction matters for batch data processing.

scenes.heading: When to use each
bullets: Job: a one-off backfill or migration
CronJob: a nightly ETL run on a schedule
backoffLimit: cap how many retries occur
scenes.narration: Reach for a Job when you have a one-off task like a backfill or a schema migration. Use a CronJob when the work must repeat on a schedule, such as a nightly ETL run. Parallelism lets a Job process multiple data shards at once. And the backoff limit caps retries so a broken task does not loop forever.

scenes.heading: A nightly CronJob
scenes.code:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-etl
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          containers:
            - name: etl
              image: myrepo/etl:1.4.0
              command: ["python", "run_etl.py"]
scenes.narration: This CronJob runs every night at two in the morning, using standard cron syntax for the schedule. The forbid concurrency policy ensures a new run never starts if the previous one is still going, which prevents overlapping ETL jobs. The job template sets a backoff limit of three retries and a restart policy of never, so a failed pod is retried by the Job controller rather than restarted in place.

scenes.heading: CronJob execution lifecycle
scenes.narration: When the schedule fires, the CronJob controller creates a fresh Job. That Job in turn spawns a pod to do the actual work. The pod runs your ETL script to completion, and its success or failure is recorded so you have a full history of every scheduled run.

scenes.text: Use Jobs for run-to-completion tasks and CronJobs for schedules, and always set backoffLimit and a concurrency policy.
scenes.narration: Choose Jobs for run-to-completion work and CronJobs for recurring schedules, and always configure a backoff limit and concurrency policy to keep batch data workloads safe.
